=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml:129-131, 154-158 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The alert-silencing gates still use the issue title (`[E2E ...]`) as the initial trigger and add a trusted-author check (user.type == "User" AND author_association IN OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR). The issue recommendation states "Require verified release-fixture provenance before silencing alerts; do not use an author-controlled title as the suppression criterion." The PR's approach still uses the author-controlled title as part of the suppression criterion — it just adds an author check. A trusted author (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR) can still create an arbitrary `[E2E ...]` issue and silence alerts. Verified release-fixture provenance would require checking for a specific release-workflow marker (e.g., a specific label, a specific author like `github-actions[bot]`, or a specific marker in the issue body that only the release gate creates).
  WHY: An attacker or mistaken trusted collaborator creates an issue titled `[E2E Clarify Negative Test] malicious` — the gate matches the title, verifies the author is trusted, and silences alerts. Worker failures or escalations then send no Telegram alert, creating the exact failure mode the security finding warned about.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Require verified release-fixture provenance before silencing alerts; do not use an author-controlled title as the suppression criterion."
  Expected change site: All workflows that set ALERT_MSG_LEVEL=SILENT based on `[E2E ...]` title patterns: orchestrate.yml:104-106, implement.yml:142-144 and 175-177 and 1672-1675, plan.yml:505-506 and 531-533 and 544, review_autofix.yml:3515-3516 and 3561
  Evidence of absence: The PR only fixes clarify.yml and orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml. The other five workflows (orchestrate.yml, implement.yml at three sites, plan.yml at two sites, review_autofix.yml) still set ALERT_MSG_LEVEL=SILENT based solely on title patterns without any provenance check. An untrusted author can create an issue titled `[E2E ...]` in those workflows and silence alerts the same way. The issue recommendation is general ("do not use an author-controlled title as the suppression criterion") but the PR only addresses two of the seven affected workflows.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus
